rules.text: Layout tokens store **parameters only**: base unit, scale ratio, fluid minimum and maximum width, density multipliers, minimum track sizes, aspect ratios. Every size step is generated from them.
Generated steps are never edited by hand; CI fails if a generated file differs from what the parameters produce.
The fluid range is **320px to 1440px**. Below 320px nothing shrinks further; above 1440px sizes stop growing and the grid adds space instead.
Stored dimensions use the DTCG `dimension` shape, `{ "value": n, "unit": "px" | "rem" }`. The fluid `clamp()` expressions exist only in generated CSS.
Layout tokens are registered with `@property` (type `<length>`, `<number>` or `<ratio>`), so an invalid value is rejected by CSS itself.
The base is **1rem = 16px** (the browser default). Tokens are written in `rem`; 16px is only used to convert design values.
The root font size is never set in `px`. If `html` sets a font size at all, it is `100%`, so a user's browser font-size setting still scales the whole interface.
The spacing step is **0.25rem (4px at the default size)**. Every spacing value, gap, padding and control height is a whole multiple of it, after density is applied and before rounding.
Spacing is a curated set of **9 named steps** (working names 3xs, 2xs, xs, s, m, l, xl, 2xl, 3xl until the naming contract), not open multiples. Only these steps can be used.

All 9 steps are generated by **one formula** from the same parameters (the 0.25rem step, a growth ratio of **1.5** (the largest step at 1440px is 1.5× its size at 320px), the 320–1440px range). Growth scales with the size of the step, so small steps barely change and large steps grow most. There are no fixed exceptions. Results are rounded to the 0.25rem step.
Usage names (inset, squish and stretch inset, stack, inline) point to a step; they never hold their own values.
Density never adds or removes spacing steps; it changes the relations between them (L-D1).

**rem owns the system, em owns the inside of a component.** rem: type scale, the 9 spacing steps, gaps between components, layout tracks, container thresholds, floors. em: block and inline insets, icon size beside text, icon-to-label gap.

The bridge from rem to em is a set of **unitless ratio tokens** (e.g. block inset = ratio × the component's own text size × density). A component's padding is a relation to its own text, and its text comes from the rem type scale.
`em` is used only **one level deep**, on a component's own properties. Nested parts take their size from a rem token, never from a chain of ems, so sizes can't compound.

**No raw px values are stored anywhere, including accessibility floors.** A floor is a ratio of the base, stored as an alias under the compliance level: target minimum = 6 steps in AA, 11 steps in AAA. At the default size these equal 24px and 44px.
A floor is applied inside the formula (`max(value, floor)`), so a size can never be generated below it. A checker never patches a value afterwards.

Floors follow the user's browser text size, because they are in `rem`. If a user deliberately sets text smaller than 16px, the floor shrinks with it; we respect that choice and add no px safety value. CI tests floors at the default 16px and at larger text sizes.
Every fluid `clamp()` mixes `rem` with a viewport or container unit in its middle term; viewport-only or container-only sizing is not allowed.
For fluid **text**, the largest size is at most **2.5×** the smallest, so text still reaches 200% under zoom.
Generated sizes are rounded to the base grid with `round()`, so no layout value lands on a fraction of a pixel.
Every fluid size is tested at 200% and 400% browser zoom on the docs site.
Component styles contain **no viewport `@media` width or height queries**. Components respond to their container with `@container`.
There are no named breakpoints. A layout switch happens at a **calculated threshold**, the sum of the minimum track sizes involved, never at a device number.
Flexible grid tracks use `minmax(0, 1fr)`, not bare `1fr`, so long content can't force a track wider than its container.
Flex and grid children that hold text set `min-width: 0` (or `min-inline-size: 0`) so long words wrap instead of overflowing.
Space between siblings comes only from `gap` with a spacing token. No margins between items inside a primitive.
Only logical properties and values are used (`margin-inline-start`, `inset-inline-end`, `inline-size`…); physical ones (`left`, `margin-right`, `width` for inline sizing) are rejected by lint.
Use grid when the container sets the structure, and flexbox when the content sets the size along one axis.
Full-height surfaces use `dvh` (or `svh` / `lvh`), never `100vh`, so mobile browser bars don't cut off content.
Edge-to-edge surfaces add `env(safe-area-inset-*)` to their padding.
The `order` property and `row-reverse` / `column-reverse` are not used on content.
Grid placement never puts items in a visual order that differs from the source order.
`reading-flow` is not relied on, because it isn't Baseline.
The layout system provides nine primitives: **stack, cluster, switcher, sidebar, grid, shell, frame, reel, center**.
Components and generated pages compose primitives; they don't write their own layout CSS for something a primitive covers.
Each primitive takes only token parameters (spacing step, minimum size, ratio, threshold), never raw values.
Every primitive establishes a container (`container-type: inline-size`) so its children can respond to it.
**Reel** (horizontal scroll) is keyboard-focusable, has an accessible name, and uses scroll snap.
**Frame** sets `aspect-ratio` from a ratio token, so space is reserved before media loads.
**Center** caps the reading width: about 65 characters by default, and at most 80 characters in the AAA theme.
The shell exposes its regions as landmarks: `banner`, `navigation`, `main` (exactly one), `complementary` where used, `contentinfo`.
The shell's first focusable element is a skip link to `main`.
Sticky headers and footers set `scroll-padding` to their own size, so focused elements are never covered (fully covered in AA, partly covered in AAA).
The navigation changes form (side navigation to menu button) at a calculated threshold: navigation minimum width plus content minimum width.
The shell never locks orientation.
On foldables, the shell may use viewport segments to keep content off the hinge, behind `@supports` only. Without them, the container layout still works.

Density is **one value** that drives three relations: (1) it adjusts the growth ratio (compact grows less, comfortable more); (2) it scales the gaps between elements; (3) it scales **block (vertical) insets only**. Inline (horizontal) insets and icon-to-label gaps don't change.
Density levels are ratios: **compact 0.75, default 1, comfortable 1.25**.
One density applies to a whole page or scope; densities are never mixed inside one hierarchy.
The user's chosen density is stored and always wins over tenant and device defaults.

No density setting can make an interactive target smaller than the **target-minimum alias** for the active compliance level (L-T14). CI verifies the computed result is at least 24 × 24 CSS px (AA) or 44 × 44 CSS px (AAA).
When the user's main pointer is coarse (`pointer: coarse`), the default density is "comfortable".
When the user asks for more contrast (`prefers-contrast: more`), the AAA theme is selected by default.
An explicit choice by the user or tenant always overrides these defaults.
Nothing is reachable only on hover; every hover affordance also works by focus and by tap.
At 320 CSS px wide, no page scrolls sideways. Only data tables, code blocks and diagrams may scroll, each inside its own scroll container.
Layouts survive the WCAG 1.4.12 text-spacing overrides (line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2×, letter spacing 0.12em, word spacing 0.16em) with no clipped or overlapping text.
Every layout is tested in both `dir="ltr"` and `dir="rtl"`, with mixed-direction content.
Direction-specific styling uses `:dir(rtl)` / `:dir(ltr)`, not `[dir]` attribute selectors.
Docs-site pages keep Cumulative Layout Shift at or below 0.1.
Core layout uses only Baseline features (newly or widely available).
Any non-Baseline feature sits inside `@supports`, and the layout still works without it.
